text: Lesson 52 already covered Expectations in Python, in full — three enforcement levels, one line each. This lesson assumes that and adds the SQL side.
A CONSTRAINT clause, declared right inside a CREATE STREAMING TABLE statement, is the SQL equivalent of Lesson 52's @dp.expect decorators — same three levels: warn, drop, or fail.
EXPECT alone defaults to warn. ON VIOLATION DROP ROW filters the row out. ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE stops the entire pipeline run — the exact same outcomes as Lesson 52's Python decorators.
A manual quality check is a separate query kept in sync by hand. A CONSTRAINT rule lives inside the table's own definition — the check and the transformation can never drift apart.
Same engine, same three outcomes, SQL syntax instead of a decorator. Next up: deploying a pipeline definition as code with Databricks Asset Bundles.
